## 30-minute project start

Write a README with the objective, intended output, owner, authoritative location, current status, likely data sources, and immediate restrictions. Record the next decision, the person who can make it, and whether a separate charter is warranted. Do not start analysis while ownership, source identity, restrictions, or intended outputs remain materially unclear.

## Choose the pathway

### Standard project start

Use [Plan](../practices/plan/index.qmd) and [Project scope](../practices/plan/project-scope.qmd) to define purpose, boundaries, outputs, roles, and completion criteria. Then use [Data-management planning](../practices/plan/data-management-planning.qmd) before receiving data.

### Higher-consequence project

Use the same sequence with a standalone [project charter](../templates/project-charter-template.md), explicit review authority, data-management decisions, environment planning, and a documented handoff expectation. Triggers include publication intent, operational use, sensitive or governed data, substantial computation, formal deliverables, or consequential policy use.

### When data arrive

Use [Data intake](../practices/acquire/data-intake.qmd) before correcting, renaming, normalizing, or accepting the delivery. Use [Recurring and programmatic data](../practices/acquire/recurring-programmatic-data.qmd) for APIs, databases, and scheduled retrievals.

## Compact initiation checklist

- [ ] Objective, intended output, owner, location, and status are in the README.
- [ ] Scope boundaries, dependencies, and completion criteria are stated.
- [ ] Roles, decision authority, data contacts, and restrictions are identified.
- [ ] Storage, computing, acquisition, and handoff conditions are plausible.
- [ ] The project uses the [readiness checklist](../templates/project-readiness-checklist.md) at initiation.
